summary: US-023c: Inventory implements schema 5 and projects seat adjacency
description:
**Third slice of TKT-175.** The producer change and the projection — still with **no rule enforced**.

**Scope narrowed during TKT-180's ai-review:** catalog's emission moved to **TKT-183**. A shared merge does not order a deployment — catalog and inventory start independently — so the producer needs its own revision, deployed after this one. This ticket is inventory-only.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Inventory, handling schema 5, fetches `GET /public/seat-maps/{id}` for that **exact immutable version** before opening its transaction, converts position-ordered rows into left/right adjacency (null = row end), and commits the pool, the flag, the projection and `consumed_events` **atomically**.
- [ ] Resolution failure fails closed: delayed NAK, **no pool provisioned**. A partial or malformed geometry is never stored.
- [ ] Adjacency is derived from each row's `position` order — not label arithmetic, which breaks on non-numeric labels and position gaps. Sections and rows never connect.
- [ ] Provisioning is idempotent on the event id, like today's.
- [ ] **No claim behaviour changes.** Seat claims on an enabled pool behave exactly as they do now.

Quality gates: `make check` green; the schema-4 golden unchanged; provisioning atomicity and idempotency tested against real Postgres.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` ... Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: The architecture, every design decision and the full test plan live in TKT-175's kind=plan and kind=plan-final — read those first, they are not repeated here

governingAdrs.why: The fetch targets the EXACT published version the pool is seated against, never the family's current one — resolving the family would silently re-point a live pool's topology. This immutability is what makes a one-time projection safe.
The producer half: bump on consumer semantics, and only now that TKT-180 has landed the consumers. The schema-4 golden must stay byte-identical for rule-off maps.
The geometry fetch happens BEFORE the inventory transaction opens. A network call inside the claim transaction is what this architecture exists to avoid.
The projection is queried per pool at claim time in the next slice; index it now and prove the scan, not just the result.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Readiness — PASS

The largest of the four and still one slice: one producer change, one consumer path, one projection, no behaviour change to defend. Its correctness is provable by 'the pool now has a projection' plus 'nothing else moved'.

Shaping is inherited: TKT-175's `kind=plan` (gpt-5.6-sol) and `kind=plan-final` (main-agent) decided the architecture, the design, the test plan and the risks before this ticket existed. This child re-scopes delivery, not thinking.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-181

Third slice of TKT-175. Blocker TKT-180 merged (`3159ead8`). Branch off `origin/main`. Gateless under the standing waiver; planning inherited from TKT-175's `kind=plan-final` and ADR-041.

**Stop-condition pre-check:** one additive migration (a pool flag + the adjacency table, guarded Down) — anticipated by ADR-041. No auth, no money, no CI config. No claim behaviour changes and nothing emits schema 5, so the slice is inert by construction.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implementation — TKT-181

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**. PR [#151](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/151) · four commits.

Inventory reads the orphan-prevention seated fork and — unlike the arm TKT-180 deliberately removed — arrives with the projection that makes accepting it honest. Geometry for the exact immutable published version is fetched **once, before the transaction**, flattened into per-seat left/right neighbours from each row's `position` order, and committed atomically with the pool, the flag and `consumed_events`.

Rule-off does no work at all, proven by absence: no fetch, no projection row, both read back as zero.

The four commits are one feature and three rounds of corrections — see the ai-review summary.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial code review — TKT-181

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`**, per `config.models.aiReview`. Cross-model check holds. **Three passes — churn cap.** Findings **3 → 2 → 2**, all real, all fixed, each pass finding defects the previous pass's fix introduced.

**Every finding after the first was about one distinction: a dependency outage versus corrupt data.**

#### Pass 1

- **[critical] A catalog blip terminated the publication.** The disposition branch retried only schema 1, so a timeout or 5xx classified every schema-5 event as poison: gone for ever, slot left with no inventory. **The code claimed the opposite two lines away** — the kind of comment that stops anyone checking.
- **[high] The correction wave could not upgrade an existing pool.** `ON CONFLICT(slot_id) DO NOTHING` would leave a pre-transport pool rule-off, insert adjacency beside it, and consume the fresh event — the organizer's rule silently disabled by the mechanism meant to repair it.
- **[high] Malformed geometry could commit partially.** Omitted positions decode as zero, duplicate positions make sort order arbitrary, identities were deduplicated raw but trimmed only for emptiness.

#### Pass 2 — the fix over-corrected

- **[high] Every geometry error became retryable**, so deterministically-corrupt geometry parked for ever. The mirror image of the bug just fixed.
- **[high] A valid JSON prefix followed by garbage** decoded the prefix and committed it as authoritative — permanently, since the same transaction consumes the event.

#### Pass 3 — the line was in the wrong place twice

- **[high] An interrupted body read looked like a syntax error.** A transport can succeed through the headers and fail mid-body; the decoder returns unexpected EOF and the event was terminated — a publication deleted because a connection dropped. The body is now buffered (bounded) before decoding.
- **[high] A blanket 4xx sweep** sent 408, 425, 429 and 401 to termination. Only **404 and 410** — catalog's settled answer that this map is not there — are deterministic now.

#### The lesson

Three passes on one boolean. First everything terminated, then everything retried, then the boundary was drawn wrong twice. **The default must be retry, with permanence as a narrow enumerated exception:** a needless retry costs a delay, a wrong terminate costs the publication.

#### Verification

Every fix mutation-verified. The resolver had **no tests whatsoever** until pass 1 said so; it now has real `httptest` coverage for the derivation and every malformed shape — including a server that promises a `Content-Length` and then stops, because a buffered test body cannot exhibit a mid-read failure, and a table that asserts the error **type** rather than merely that an error occurred (the earlier version passed whichever way the failure was classified, which was exactly the bug).

`make check` green after all four commits and on merged `main`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-181 (self-validated under the waived Gate 4)

Merged `97562a0c` (squash of PR #151). `make check` re-run on merged `main` → `EXIT=0`.

| AC | Met | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Inventory handles schema 5 and provisions the projection atomically | ✅ | `TestProvisionSeatedCommitsAdjacencyAtomically`; the store refuses a rule-enabled pool with no projection. |
| Geometry fetched for the **exact** published version, before the transaction | ✅ | Resolver rejects a wrong map id and a draft status; the fetch happens in `provisionInput`, outside the store transaction. |
| Adjacency from `position` order; row ends explicit | ✅ | `TestSeatMapAdjacencyDerivesNeighboursFromPosition` (gaps are spacing, not missing seats) and `…NeverConnectsRowsOrSections`. |
| Failure fails closed, nothing partial stored | ✅ | Nine malformed shapes refused, each asserting the error **type**; provisioning refuses an enabled pool without a projection. |
| Idempotent, and upgrades an existing pool | ✅ | `…UpgradesAnExistingPool`, `…RuleFlagIsMonotonic`, `…RefusesToAdoptAMismatchedPool`. |
| **No claim behaviour changes** | ✅ | Claim path untouched; full inventory smoke suite green. |
| Rule off costs nothing | ✅ | `…RuleOffWritesNoProjection` plus a consumer test whose resolver errors if called at all. |

#### The honest part

The first commit was inert and looked finished. Three review rounds found seven real defects in it, **six of them about one boolean** — retry or terminate — and two of those were introduced by my own fixes. The critical one shipped with a comment asserting the opposite of what the code did.

#### Newly unblocked

**TKT-182** — the rule itself.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closeout — TKT-181

Merged `97562a0c` · PR [#151](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/151) · branch deleted.

#### Durations

| Stage | Duration |
|---|---|
| Backlog → Ready (created in TKT-175's split) | ~2h 20m |
| Building — coding + **3 review passes** + 5 gate runs | ~1h 15m |
| **Total Ready → merged** | **~1h 15m** |

`human-wait total`: **0s** — gateless.

#### Diff

`+868 / −49 (13 files)`.

#### Learnings

1. **Retry-vs-terminate is one boolean and it took three review passes.** The safe default is asymmetric: a needless retry costs a delay, a wrong terminate costs the event. Permanence must be a narrow enumerated list, never a range. → **`docs/LEARNINGS.md`**.
2. **Decode from a buffer, not from the response body**, or an interrupted transport is indistinguishable from malformed content — and they need opposite dispositions. → **`docs/LEARNINGS.md`**.
3. **A comment asserting a disposition is not evidence of it.** The critical finding sat two lines under a comment claiming the opposite. → the fix is a disposition test per branch, which now exists.
4. **`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` cannot tell a replay from an upgrade.** Both look like "the row exists". If a correction wave can ever re-emit under a fresh id, the write path needs an explicit upgrade branch with identity verification. → **`docs/LEARNINGS.md`**.
5. **An HTTP boundary with no tests is invisible until something decodes badly.** The resolver had none; the doubles returned well-formed Go slices and proved nothing about parsing. → **`docs/LEARNINGS.md`**.

#### Newly unblocked

**TKT-182** (the rule) → then **TKT-183** (catalog emits + the correction wave).

#### retro

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

- **The disposition should have been designed, not inherited.** I added a catalog call inside `provisionInput` without asking what the existing branch did with an error from it — and the existing branch was written when only schema 1 called catalog. *Concrete:* when adding a dependency call to an existing handler, read that handler's failure disposition **first** and state which branch the new failure takes.
- **Three passes on one boolean is the run's clearest evidence for the cap's reset clause.** Passes 2 and 3 each found defects created by the previous fix. A mechanical "two and stop" would have merged with corrupt geometry parking for ever.

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **Twenty learnings now sit unwritten across seven tickets.** I have offered five times; this is the last time I will raise it as a retro item, per the skill's guidance that a recurring item should be patched rather than re-noted. *Concrete:* one commit to `docs/LEARNINGS.md`, direct to the default branch.
- **Two tickets remain in this epic: TKT-182 (the rule, with the contention proof) and TKT-183 (catalog emits + the correction wave).** Both inherit ADR-041, which is now correct after four amendments. They are the resumption point.
